items.action: Upgrade SonicOS to the fixed builds now; check whether any alternate login methods (local, RADIUS, LDAP) sit alongside SAML on your SSLVPN.
items.details: Affects SonicOS Gen7 up to 7.3.3-7015 and Gen8 up to 8.2.2-8015, only where SSLVPN uses SAML. Fixed in 7.3.4-7013 / 8.2.3-8015. SonicWall says it investigated a report of likely real-world exploitation and has published no workaround — upgrading is the only fix. Two related management-interface flaws in the same advisory (SNWLID-2026-0014) are rated 8.8.
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-19868 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov 6: an attacker holding valid credentials for an alternate login method can bypass SAML authentication — and SAML-enforced MFA — on SonicWall SonicOS SSLVPN. US federal agencies must remediate by Nov 20.
items.title: SonicWall SSLVPN MFA bypass is exploited — patch before Nov 20

items.action: Update Paint via Microsoft Store > Library > Get updates, or run: winget upgrade --id 9PCFS5B6T72H --source msstore. Verify build 11.2609.401.0 or later.
items.details: The out-of-bounds read (CWE-125) was disclosed Oct 13; Microsoft revised the advisory on Nov 6 to name build 11.2609.401.0 as the fix, then on Nov 7 lowered the CVSS score from 8.1 to 7.0 (local vector, user interaction required), calling it an informational change. No exploitation has been reported and no public exploit exists.
items.summary: Microsoft's fix for the Paint remote code execution flaw CVE-2026-83844 ships only through the Microsoft Store, as Paint build 11.2609.401.0. Installing the October Windows update does not patch it, so fleets relying on WSUS or Windows Update are still exposed.
items.title: Windows Paint RCE fix is Store-only — Windows Update won't deliver it

items.action: Upgrade OpenAM to 16.1.4 or later and rotate session tokens on exposed deployments.
items.details: Published Nov 8. A fix is available in OpenAM 16.1.4 and later. Session-token disclosure can let an attacker hijack authenticated sessions outright, so exposed deployments should be treated as potentially compromised until patched and sessions rotated.
items.summary: CVE-2026-123551 lets unauthenticated attackers read live session tokens from OpenAM's notification WebSocket by bypassing the agent-only check. It affects OpenAM 14.0.0 through 16.1.3 and is rated the maximum CVSS 10.0.
items.title: OpenAM flaw (CVSS 10.0) leaks live session tokens to unauthenticated attackers

items.action: If you use Chainalysis, reset passwords, rotate API keys, and check for any KYT account access without authorization.
items.details: The company discovered the broader exposure on Nov 2 and disclosed it late Nov 4. Every user must reset passwords and rotate API keys; KYT restoration requires customers to register trusted IPs for an allowlist. Chainalysis says it has no evidence investigation data was accessed or attribution data manipulated, and has not named the actor or published a user count.
items.summary: Chainalysis now says an 'agentic' attack exposed names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all of its users — reversing its Oct 30 assurance that no credentials were touched. In its Nov 7 update, Reactor, KYT and Address Screening are back online with tighter controls, while Data Solutions and Chain (Beta) remain offline.
items.title: Chainalysis breach exposed password hashes and live tokens for all users

items.action: Treat as an unverified claim; healthcare teams should watch for the group's indicators and review backup and segmentation posture.
items.details: The claim surfaced Nov 8. The alleged haul includes MD5-hashed staff credentials, 691,000 admissions, 34.5 million medical-history rows and 1.5 million invoices. No independently verified evidence of data exfiltration or disruption to clinical services has been published.
items.summary: The WhiteArmor ransomware group claims it breached Clínica La Sagrada Familia in Colombia, alleging it holds 254,670 patient identities plus ~598.7 million rows of clinical, financial and identity data, and is demanding $2 million in Bitcoin. The claim is unverified.
items.title: WhiteArmor claims Colombian hospital, alleges 254,670 patient identities stolen

items.action: Monitor for confirmation and for any published data; treat the listing as a claim, not a confirmed breach.
items.details: The listing is an unverified threat-actor claim at this stage. LockBit 5.0 has been one of the most active ransomware operations through 2026.
items.summary: LockBit 5.0 listed Grupo Telles, a Brazilian agricultural company, as a new victim on its leak site on Nov 8, according to ThreatMon. No independently verified information on the intrusion, data volume or operational impact has been published.
items.title: LockBit 5.0 lists Brazilian agricultural firm Grupo Telles

items.action: Yatra users should change passwords and enable 2FA; Yatra account holders should watch for credential-stuffing and phishing using the exposed data.
items.details: The report also cites 34 compromised employee credentials and 43 third-party employee credentials, with the company's external attack surface measured at 117. The leak-site listing itself gives no details on how the incident occurred or whether systems were encrypted; the data-theft claim is unverified.
items.summary: LockBit5 published Yatra.com, the Gurugram-based online travel agency, as a new victim on its leak site on Nov 8. Hudson Rock infostealer data linked to the incident shows 24,829 compromised user accounts, 84,364 passwords and 15,316 cookies.
items.title: LockBit5 lists Yatra.com; infostealer data exposes 24,829 user accounts

items.action: SBI customers should stay alert for phishing and fraudulent loan applications using KYC details; report suspicious messages to the bank and to 1930.
items.details: The exposed data reportedly included registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email and residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers and loan/lead metadata. SBI has begun notifying affected customers and says the incident had no material impact on core operations. The bank is also leading an Indian Banks' Association effort on AI-era cybersecurity strategy.
items.summary: SBI chairman C.S. Setty says the bank is stepping up cybersecurity with AI tools, API sweeps and vulnerability assessments after its Oct 21 disclosure that a cyberattack exposed personally identifiable information of 3,897 customers on the dark web. Root-cause analysis is still underway.
items.title: SBI steps up AI defences after dark-web exposure of 3,897 customer records
